answers.justification: The only evidence of an efficiency decline is the dashboard ratio (E2, C12), and its 'cooling delivered' input depends on FT-201, which was given an unverified default factor on 2 Apr 2026 (C6); against a decline, condenser-water temperature is flat and there are no high-pressure alarms (C9, C4), while the vendor's approach comparison has no matching load (E3).

Interim HX-F1 (up to 400 kW) was tied into the header just as presses moved in Apr–Jun (C11), and CH-3 run-hours doubled under an unchanged staging rule (C5, E6, C15), but there is no heat meter, the valve positions are unrecorded and a parallel cooler exists (C11), so the added load has not been measured.
The independent revenue meter rose by the same ~218 MWh, and its accuracy test passed (C1, E1); non-chiller submeters were flat (C13); and more chiller run-hours confirm real consumption (C5).
2026 was slightly cooler and drier: lower dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures, fewer hours above 20 °C wet-bulb and 2% fewer CDD (C2, E1).
The setpoint was only lowered for 14–17 Mar and then restored, the parameter audit confirms 7.0 °C and the mean supply temperature was 7.1 °C (E5, C10).
An efficiency decline itself has not been established, because the dashboard ratio rests on an unverified flowmeter (C6, E2), so not even a real association can be shown.

The HX-F1 tie-in and the staged press moves (C11) line up in time with the Apr–Jun ramp (E1) and with heavier chiller staging (C5), but no heat or flow measurement on the branch confirms it caused the growth.
The setpoint change lasted 3 days in March and was reversed, with supply temperature unchanged in Apr–Oct (E5, C10), while the growth began in April and kept rising.

Only the vendor asserts the link (E3); the water-treatment records show acceptable control with a minor scaling index in Jul–Aug (C3), nobody has inspected the tubes (C7), and the efficiency decline itself is unestablished (C6).
The decisive unknowns are the true header flow (C6) and the load on the HX-F1 branch (C11); a verified temporary meter, branch logging and per-chiller power measurements resolve both at low cost.

Fouling is unconfirmed: there are no high-pressure alarms and condenser-water temperature is flat (C4, C9), the approach comparison has no matching load (E3), CH-2 was just brushed (C7) and the routine brushing is due Feb 2027.
Production needs 7 °C supply; a past drift to 8.5 °C caused scrap and missed deliveries (E4), and line 3 already complains of warm water (C15).
It is cheap and fits the already-booked Dec CH-2 outage (C7), but CH-2's tubes were brushed in Oct 2026, so the inspection gives little information about fouling on CH-1 or CH-3.
Neither the efficiency explanation nor the load explanation can be established without verified flow and branch-load data (C6, C11), so committing to substantive action is not yet justified.

ambiguousItems: S2: unknown vs supported — C11 timing, the doubled CH-3 run-hours (C5) and flat condenser conditions (C9, C4) give a fairly strong circumstantial case for added load, but the load was never measured.
S6: unknown vs association-only — the dashboard efficiency ratio co-moves with electricity, but only by construction from a suspect flowmeter.
S13: acceptable vs preferred — it costs little and is already scheduled, but the next outage is CH-2, which was just brushed.
S7: association-only vs unknown, depending on whether timing alone counts as association.
caseProblems: Internal tension: if the HX-F1 load ramped up from April to June, a header meter with a constant (default-factor) error would not show delivered cooling flat year on year month after month (E2). The case does not explain how FT-201 hides a ramping load, for example by saying where HX-F1 ties in relative to FT-201 and TT-202.

Monthly growth keeps rising through Sep–Oct (E1, E2) even though hall-coil load from Building F should fall in autumn; this is only plausible as a percentage effect against a falling baseline and is not explained.

A4's 'next scheduled single-chiller outage' is the CH-2 outage, but CH-2 was brushed in Oct 2026 (C7). This undercuts A4's diagnostic value in a way that depends on reading the catalogue closely; it may be intended, but it is subtle.
C6's catalogue title ('Calibration certificates and work-order history for chilled-water header flowmeter FT-201') makes clear that the flowmeter is the crux, which partly leaks the answer.

rulings.explanation: The key's 'unknown' can be defended. C11 records manual HX-F1 isolation and selector valves whose positions have not been recorded since commissioning, the Building C cooler is piped in parallel, and there is no heat meter, so nothing shows heat entering the loop. But this task defines 'supported' comparatively: the evidence 'supports the claim more than its rivals.' On that reading, 'supported' is also defensible. H3, H4 and H5 are contradicted. H1's support is gone: C6 invalidates the dashboard, and E3 is one approach reading from an interested vendor that is not load-matched. H2, by contrast, has positive evidence. C11 documents a physical tie-in with flow observed on 8 Apr. The hall coils have no other cooling source in C11: the parallel Building C cooler serves only the mould units, and the hall in Building C had no cooling. The three dated press moves line up with the +4/+9/+14% ramp. The ~220 kW needed fits within HX-F1's 400 kW. C5 and E6 show more chiller staging. With nothing comparable on the H1 side, a careful analyst can reasonably conclude H2 is better supported than every rival. The hall-coil load in particular has no alternative route in the current evidence, which keeps 'supported' alive despite Revision 2.
rulings.fix: Edit C11 so the heat input is genuinely open on both routes. Add: 'Facilities email 18 Jun: hall AHUs running ventilation-only (coil valves closed) pending AC-F1; not BMS-monitored, no later record.' Also add: 'Building C cooler rated for all 18 presses.' Keep 'valve stroked, flow observed' and the press-move dates, so S7 stays association-only. After this edit, whether any heat reaches the central loop depends entirely on unrecorded valve positions, and S2 = unknown is uniquely defensible.

rulings.explanation: R1 needs a decline in chiller efficiency to be shown co-occurring with the electricity growth. The only series showing an efficiency decline is the dashboard kWe/kWr ratio. Its numerator is the MCC-4 electricity itself, and its denominator comes from FT-201, which C6 invalidates in both periods: open drift work order, verification last done in 2022, and a default calibration factor with no wet check since April 2026. Its co-movement with electricity is therefore partly by construction, and it is not independent evidence that efficiency fell. C12 only repeats the dashboard. E3 is one CH-1 approach reading, not load-matched, compared with a start-up value at unknown load; that is not a time series and cannot show covariation. E6 is a subjective impression. Because the 'from' condition is not shown to have occurred, co-occurrence cannot be shown. 'Unknown' fits the definition ('insufficient even to show association'), and 'association-only' would mean accepting an invalidated instrument.

A4 means opening a waterbox at 'the next scheduled single-chiller service outage'. C7 identifies that as CH-2's outage on 8–10 Dec, and CH-2's tubes were brushed on 24–27 Oct with no record of their condition. A visual check would show about six weeks of deposit on a freshly cleaned unit. It would tell little about CH-1, the unit the vendor measured, or CH-3, neither opened since Feb 2025. It cannot address the competing explanation, HX-F1 load growth. It is cheap and harmless, so 'acceptable', but clearly weaker than A1, which separates the two explanations directly. 'Preferred' is therefore not defensible. One small risk: C7's planner note says only that 'a waterbox could be opened', which a reader might take to include CH-1's waterbox during the low-load December window.
rulings.fix: Optional tightening: in C7, change 'a waterbox could be opened' to 'the CH-2 condenser waterbox could be opened', so no reader can assume CH-1 is inspectable in that window.

rulings.explanation: R2's 'from' condition is a heat load connected to the chilled-water loop, and C11 documents that connection. HX-F1 was tied into the central header for loads that were not on the central loop in Building C, with flow observed at commissioning on 8 Apr. The three dated relocation phases (8 Apr, 13 May, 10 Jun) track the E1 ramp of +4%, +9% and +14%. This is co-occurrence plus covariation in stages, more than bare timing, so 'unknown' understates the evidence. 'Causal' is not justified: the heat transferred is unmeasured, the valve positions are unrecorded, a parallel cooler exists, and the efficiency rival is not ruled out. 'Contradicted' fails because C11 refutes the manager's denial in E4. 'Association-only' is the only defensible answer.
rulings.fix: No change needed. If the S2 fix is adopted, keep the commissioning note 'valve stroked, flow observed' and the press-move dates so this ruling stays unchanged.
